identity.real_world_identity_notes: Historical evidence says most DBR9s used a six-speed sequential gearbox while some used an H-pattern manual. Exact AMS2 cockpit inspection resolves this representation to a sequential stick without paddles.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a round rim without an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car stalled when moving from rest without physical clutch input.
All six sequential-stick gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts with automatic throttle cut.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted and no automatic throttle blip was observed; authentic rev matching therefore requires the driver to blip the throttle manually.
AMS2's generic acceptance of direct gear inputs on sequential cars is not recorded as a car-specific characteristic.
The exact Low Downforce identity inherits the verified base controls as an approved aero-package assumption and was not separately live-tested.
Base car live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Standing-start clutch, six-speed sequential stick without paddles, automatic cut, no automatic blip, and round no-display rim were directly observed.
Low Downforce inherits the base controls as an approved aero-package assumption and was not separately live-tested.

confidence.basis: Exact simulator identity, modeled hardware, and shift behavior were directly tested; historical evidence supports the six-speed sequential family while preserving the known DBR9 variant caveat.

claims.basis: Official release context and exact live CarModel/class observation establish the simulated identity.
